Apple just turned AI into a default operating system layer — and Google helped build it.

At WWDC 2026, Apple announced AFM 3: a family of five foundation models that run across every Apple device and Apple's cloud infrastructure. The on-device models include a 3B dense model and a 20B sparse multimodal model using a new technique called Instruction-Following Pruning — meaning advanced AI reasoning happens directly on your phone without data ever leaving the device. A confirmed $1 billion Gemini license deal with Google powers the cloud tier.

This matters for every business leader, not just those in the Apple ecosystem. When the world's largest consumer hardware company ships native AI in every product, the baseline expectation for intelligent software rises across the board. If you are building apps, managing device fleets, or delivering digital products to consumers, your users now compare your experience against what comes free with their iPhone.

The deeper shift is architectural. Apple is treating foundation models the way it once treated the camera or GPS — as platform infrastructure that every developer builds on top of. That changes product strategy, privacy architecture, and competitive positioning simultaneously.
